analysisMarkdown:
## Where the price sits

Spot gold trades at **$3,547.75 per ounce**, down a sharp **4.80%** over the past 24 hours. That move leaves the metal sitting right on its **52-week low of $3,548** (set today, 2026-11-20) and **35.4% below the 52-week high of $5,496** recorded on 2026-01-29. This is not record territory — it is the opposite end of the year's range.

The trend picture is uniformly soft. Spot is **12.1% below its 50-day average** of $4,037 and **16.4% below its 200-day average** of $4,244. Momentum has been negative across every lookback: **-9.0% over 20 days**, **-22.9% over 90 days**, and **-12.9% over the past year**. The 20-day closing range runs from $3,595 to $4,121, so today's price has broken beneath even the low end of that recent band. With 20-day annualised volatility at **32%**, daily swings of this size are consistent with an unsettled, trending-lower tape.

## The macro backdrop

Two forces dominate, and both lean against gold.

- **The dollar.** The Federal Reserve's trade-weighted **broad dollar index** stands at **122.65**, up 0.65 over 30 days and 3.75 over 90 days. It is now **higher than 100% of readings in the past year** — a one-year high. A firmer dollar makes gold more expensive for buyers outside the United States and is a classic headwind.
- **Real yields.** The **10-year real yield** is **2.88%**, up 0.08 pp over 30 days and 0.53 pp over 90 days, **higher than 96% of the past year's readings**. Because gold pays no income, elevated real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding it.

Around these, the **10-year Treasury yield** sits at **5.07%** (down 0.08 pp over 30 days but up 0.38 pp over 90 days), and the **10-year inflation breakeven** has eased to **2.19%** (down 0.16 pp over 30 days). Softer inflation expectations alongside firm real yields are not the combination gold tends to rally on.

## The scorecard, in plain language

**Short term (1–4 weeks).** The measured factors net to a **SELL** baseline. The 20-day return of -8.98% is strongly adverse, and price sitting 12.13% under the 50-day average adds to that. The 30-day changes in real yields and the dollar register as roughly neutral. The single supportive factor is contrarian: price is now stretched far below its own 50-day average, which can limit how much further a short, sharp move extends. On balance the reading is **SELL, medium confidence**.

**Long term (3–12 months).** Here the scorecard is uniformly negative, scoring across the board. Spot is 16.41% below the 200-day average; the 50-day average is 4.87% below the 200-day (a downtrend structure); the 90-day return is -22.86%; price is 35.44% below the 52-week high; the 90-day change in real yields (+0.53 pp) is adverse; and the 90-day change in the dollar (+3.15%) is adverse. That produces a **SELL, high confidence** reading.

## Why no adjustment today

Adjustments are reserved for a specific, dated, sourced event that the scorecard cannot yet see — a central-bank decision, a data release, a geopolitical shock. I was not able to confirm any such fresh catalyst from primary reporting for this date, and the macro factors already in the data (the dollar at a one-year high, elevated real yields, eased breakevens) are precisely what the scorecard is built on. Standing conditions — persistent official-sector demand or gold's long-run diversification role — are true every day and do not qualify. The honest reading is therefore the default: **step 0 on both horizons.**

## Short-term outlook

Conditions over the next few weeks look more challenging than supportive. Price has broken below its 20-day range, momentum is firmly negative, and both the dollar and real yields are working against the metal. The one genuine counterweight is how far price has fallen beneath its 50-day average, which is why the signal is SELL rather than a deeper conviction. **A daily close above $4,121 would break this view** and force the standing call to change.

## Long-term outlook

The 3–12 month setup is the weaker of the two. Every structural and macro factor on the long-term scorecard currently points the same way: a price below both major moving averages, a bearish moving-average cross, a deep 90-day drawdown, and a backdrop of firm real yields and a strong dollar. **A daily close above $4,673 would break this view.**

## Risks to the calls

The main risk to both SELL readings is a swift reversal in the macro drivers — a meaningful retreat in the dollar from its one-year high, or a drop in real yields. A surprise dovish shift in central-bank policy, a sharp escalation in geopolitical risk, or a renewed wave of safe-haven and official-sector buying could all turn conditions more supportive quickly, and the high volatility (32% annualised) means moves can be large. Conversely, further dollar strength or higher real yields would deepen the adverse setup. The stated invalidation levels — **$4,121** short-term and **$4,673** long-term — are the lines that would formally change each standing call.
